items.title: Art Farmer — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I knew Ornette out in California in the early 50s before I left California with Lionel. We used to run into each other on jam sessions around town.

ctx.x: What was it like working with George? What was he like as a person?

George was great. George is a great musician, but the thing that really impressed me about him was that he was very patient, and he never got excited and said, “Damn, you guys are awful. You’re messing up the music. Why does it take so long?” He never said nothing like that. It was always positive. He said, “Okay, let’s take it again” [laughs]. I don’t know how many times we would take it. Looking back, it seems ironic after spending weeks practicing alone, then you get into the recording studio and you still are…
And at this time, he was developing his Lydian Chromatic Concepts.
